newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb defused in church of French Scientology.
newsitem.headline: Bomb defused in church of French Scientology.

text.p: A member of the Church of Scientology found and defused a powerful bomb on Friday in a church in the western town of Angers, police sources said.
They said the device, concealed in a sports bag, was found in the entry hall shortly after the Scientology church, near the town railway station, opened in the morning.

The Church member who found it carried it to a nearby park and defused it himself. Eyewitnesses said it had been primed to explode minutes later. "The explosive device was made to kill and was very powerful," one investigator said.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility and no indication of the motives behind the attack.
Several leaders of the French branch of the U.S.-based Church of Scientology went on trial in the central city of Lyon last November in connection with a local follower's suicide.
The Church's national leaders were acquitted. A former leader of the Church in Lyon was convicted of manslaughter and fraud and jailed for 18 months with another 18 months suspended.
At the trial, prosecutors depicted the church as a business masquerading as a religion, whose chief function was to extort cash from the gullible.
Defence lawyers said the organisation was a legitimate religion and argued that their clients were the innocent victims of a government campaign to crack down on cults.
